reference.source: GeneReviews / Smith's Recognizable Patterns of Human Malformation
clinicalPearls: A recurrent deletion generated by non-allelic homologous recombination between flanking segmental duplications, encompassing the HNF1B gene
The classic renal-endocrine phenotype is renal cysts and diabetes (RCAD): structural kidney disease with maturity-onset diabetes of the young
Renal abnormalities are common and varied, including cysts, dysplasia, hyperechogenic kidneys and collecting-system anomalies, sometimes detected antenatally
Maturity-onset diabetes of the young (HNF1B-related, historically MODY5) may present in adolescence or adulthood
Approximately 15 percent of carriers have a neurodevelopmental or psychiatric phenotype, including learning difficulty, autism or schizophrenia
Genital-tract anomalies occur, including Müllerian malformations in females, and pancreatic hypoplasia with exocrine insufficiency may be present
Point mutations or whole-gene deletion of HNF1B produce an overlapping phenotype, so a normal microarray does not exclude HNF1B disease
Chromosomal microarray is the first-line test, with renal imaging and metabolic surveillance central to management
reference.pathophysiology: The 17q12 region is flanked by segmental duplications that predispose to non-allelic homologous recombination, generating a recurrent deletion or its reciprocal duplication. The deleted interval contains HNF1B, a transcription factor essential for the development of the kidney, pancreas, liver and genital tract; its haploinsufficiency causes the renal structural abnormalities, the beta-cell dysfunction underlying maturity-onset diabetes and the Müllerian anomalies. Additional dosage-sensitive genes in the interval contribute to the neurodevelopmental phenotype seen in a minority of carriers. Deletions are frequently de novo, and expressivity is variable even within families.
additionalDifferentials: Isolated HNF1B point mutation or intragenic deletion (a common phenocopy with a normal microarray)
Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease and other cystic kidney disorders
Other monogenic (MODY) and syndromic forms of young-onset diabetes
Mayer-Rokitansky-Küster-Hauser syndrome and other causes of Müllerian aplasia
Bardet-Biedl syndrome and other cystic-kidney ciliopathies
Other recurrent copy-number syndromes causing neurodevelopmental problems
additionalInvestigations: Chromosomal microarray as first-line to detect and size the deletion
HNF1B sequencing and dosage analysis where the microarray is normal but the phenotype fits
Renal ultrasound and, where indicated, further imaging to characterise structural kidney disease
Renal function, electrolytes (including magnesium) and glucose/HbA1c with ongoing diabetes surveillance
Parental studies to establish inheritance and counsel recurrence risk
Pelvic imaging for Müllerian anomalies and developmental assessment where indicated
redFlags: Deteriorating renal function or antenatally detected severe renal malformation
New hyperglycaemia or symptoms of diabetes
Neurodevelopmental regression or emerging psychiatric symptoms
reference.prognosis: The outlook is dominated by renal and metabolic disease: kidney involvement ranges from mild cysts to progressive impairment that may reach end-stage renal failure, and diabetes often develops over time and requires long-term management. Most carriers have normal cognition, but the minority with neurodevelopmental involvement need additional support; lifelong renal and metabolic surveillance is essential.
pitfalls: Assuming a normal chromosomal microarray excludes HNF1B disease, when a point mutation or intragenic deletion can produce the same phenotype
Overlooking the diabetes risk and failing to arrange metabolic surveillance
Missing hypomagnesaemia, which is characteristic of HNF1B-related disease
Failing to investigate genital-tract anomalies in affected females
Discounting the diagnosis when neurodevelopmental features are absent, since most carriers are cognitively normal
references: Smith's Recognizable Patterns of Human Malformation
Emery and Rimoin's Principles and Practice of Medical Genetics
management: Monitor renal function and image structural kidney disease, managing chronic kidney disease and progression towards renal failure through nephrology
Manage HNF1B-related maturity-onset diabetes, which often requires insulin as sulfonylureas are less effective, with glycaemic surveillance and endocrinology input
Monitor for and replace magnesium in hypomagnesaemia and manage associated electrolyte disturbance
Treat pancreatic exocrine insufficiency with pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy where present
Assess and manage Müllerian tract anomalies in females through gynaecology
Provide developmental and psychiatric support for the minority with a neurodevelopmental phenotype
Offer genetic counselling with parental testing and recurrence-risk advice, noting many deletions are de novo
